title: Newtonian mechanics
description: Newton's laws in inertial frames, Galilean transformations, work and energy, momentum and angular momentum of particles and systems, fictitious forces in non-inertial frames.

title: Lagrangian mechanics and Hamilton's principle
description: Generalized coordinates, the Lagrangian L = T − V, the stationary-action principle and the Euler–Lagrange equations, covariance under point transformations, non-uniqueness of the Lagrangian.

title: Constraints, virtual work and Lagrange multipliers
description: Holonomic, non-holonomic and semi-holonomic (Pfaffian) constraints, virtual displacements and D'Alembert's principle, Lagrange multipliers and forces of constraint.

title: Symmetries and conservation laws
description: Cyclic coordinates and conserved momenta, Noether's theorem for continuous symmetries, the Jacobi integral and when the Hamiltonian equals the energy, scaling symmetries.

title: Central forces and the Kepler problem
description: Reduction of the two-body problem, effective potential, orbit equation, Kepler's laws, scattering and the Rutherford cross-section.

title: Small oscillations and normal modes
description: Linearisation about equilibrium, stability, the generalized eigenvalue problem for normal modes and frequencies, coupled oscillators.

title: Rigid body dynamics
description: Angular velocity, the inertia tensor and principal axes, Euler's equations, Euler angles, free and heavy symmetric tops, precession and nutation.

title: Hamiltonian mechanics
description: Legendre transformation, Hamilton's equations, phase space and Liouville's theorem, Poisson brackets and their algebra.

title: Canonical transformations, Hamilton–Jacobi theory and action–angle variables
description: Generating functions, the symplectic condition, invariance of Poisson brackets, the Hamilton–Jacobi equation, action–angle variables and integrable systems.

title: Canonical perturbation theory and the onset of chaos
description: Time-independent and time-dependent canonical perturbation theory, adiabatic invariants, resonances, the KAM picture and chaos in Hamiltonian systems.

title: Minkowski spacetime and the invariant interval
description: Events, inertial (free-float) frames, the invariant spacetime interval with signature (−,+,+,+), proper time and proper length, sign conventions across sources.

title: Lorentz transformations
description: Derivation of boosts from the principle of relativity and interval invariance, relativity of simultaneity, time dilation and length contraction as corollaries, rapidity and hyperbolic rotation, velocity addition.

title: Causal structure of Minkowski spacetime
description: Timelike, spacelike and lightlike separations, light cones, invariance of temporal order for timelike pairs, worldlines, proper time along a worldline and the twin paradox.

title: Four-vectors and the Lorentz group
description: Index notation, the Minkowski inner product, four-velocity and four-acceleration, the Lorentz group as the isometries of the interval, raising and lowering indices.

title: Relativistic momentum and energy
description: Four-momentum, E² = p²c² + m²c⁴, invariant mass of a system, conservation in collisions and decays, massless particles and thresholds.

title: The equivalence principle
description: Free-fall (locally inertial) frames, weak and Einstein equivalence principles, tidal effects as the limit of local flatness, gravitational time dilation.

title: Tensors on spacetime
description: Vectors, one-forms and (M,N) tensors as multilinear maps, coordinate bases, transformation laws, contraction, the metric and its inverse, Levi-Civita tensor and volume elements.

title: The stress-energy tensor
description: Definition and symmetry of T^{μν}, dust and perfect fluids, local conservation ∂_μ T^{μν} = 0 and its Newtonian limit, electromagnetism in geometric language.

title: Covariant derivative, parallel transport and geodesics
description: Christoffel symbols from the metric, the covariant derivative of tensors, metric compatibility, parallel transport, the geodesic equation, Lie derivatives and Killing vectors.

title: Spacetime curvature
description: The Riemann tensor from transport round a loop and from commuting covariant derivatives, its symmetries and 20 components, Ricci tensor and scalar, Bianchi identity, geodesic deviation as tides.

title: The Einstein field equation
description: The Einstein tensor and its vanishing divergence, G_{μν} = 8πG T_{μν}/c⁴ fixed by the Newtonian limit, the cosmological constant, the Einstein–Hilbert action.

title: Linearised gravity and gravitational radiation
description: Weak-field expansion g = η + h, gauge transformations, the trace-reversed perturbation and wave equation, the Newtonian limit, transverse-traceless waves, the quadrupole formula.

title: Robertson–Walker spacetimes and the Friedmann equations
description: Maximally symmetric spaces, the Robertson–Walker metric with k = −1, 0, +1, comoving coordinates, Friedmann equations, equations of state, redshift and cosmological distances.

title: Schwarzschild spacetime, relativistic stars and black holes
description: Static spherical symmetry, the Schwarzschild exterior and Birkhoff's theorem, the TOV equations, the Buchdahl limit, coordinate versus curvature singularities, horizons and orbits of light and matter.
